$$P = \left(\sqrt{rR},\; 0\right)$$

So P is the **midpoint of AB**, and PA = PB = √(rR), giving **PF² = rR** (tangent length from P to either circle).

## Using Power of a Point

**Power of H** (on tangent at F, so HF² equals power w.r.t. both circles):
- w.r.t. ω: HF² = HD · HE
- w.r.t. Ω: HF² = HB · HC

**Case 2:** R² = 84 → R = 2√21, r = 6√21, R/r = 1/3

- L = HP = PF − HF = 6√7 − 3√7 = 3√7
